text:
sophia: Heads-up — AcmeAnalytics reporting intermittent 429s and 503s from their dedicated EU2 pool. Customer says latency p95 jumps from ~180ms to 3s for short bursts. They see auth failures when bursts happen. Filing as escalation, trying to reproduce.
jen-cs: Customer attached sample request ids: req-ACME-9842, req-ACME-9847. Happened around 2025-11-02T14:12Z and 14:14Z. They say only their dedicated pool is affected, other tenants on same node fine most of the time.
infra-bot: Automated alert: node eu2-dedicated-021 reported MIG slice SM saturation event at 2025-11-02T14:11:56Z (slice_id=3). Throttle metric spike: sm_util=98%, pci_bw=80%.
mike: Can you paste the API error body for one of the 429s? Need the exact rate-limit or auth payload. Also which model + batch size?
sophia: Paste from customer: 
```json
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"slice-throttle: token budget depleted","request_id":"req-ACME-9842","status":429}
```
They were calling text-generation with model=gpt-open-std, batch=8, seq=1024.
andrew: If slice hit SM saturation it can delay kv-cache fetches and push frontends to queue requests -> auth refresh tokens time out? Could explain 503s. Need node-level perf counters and MIG partition layout.
mike: Requesting node dump: `runtimesctl node-metrics eu2-dedicated-021 --since 2m --format json` and `nvidia-smi topo --matrix` plus MIG show.
jen-cs: Customer provided partial node view: 
```
MIG partitions: 1x1g.10gb (slice0), 1x2g.20gb (slice1), 1x3g.40gb (slice3)
slice3 current tenants: acme-tenant (dedicated pool), peak sm% 97
```
Also they noted autoscaler didn't add capacity — their reserved burst policy should allow +2 slices.
infra-bot: Autoscaler attempted scale at 2025-11-02T14:11:58Z but failed: insufficient free MIG templates in region eu2 for node type a100-mig. Error: quota-exhausted.
sophia: Interesting — so autoscaler couldn't provision extra capacity and the slice hit sustained SM saturation. That matches customer burst -> 429s. Need to confirm if other tenant workloads on same slice caused noise or if acme's own burst patterns are spiky.
mike: Ask customer for perf trace around those req ids: `X-Redwood-Trace: req-ACME-9842`. Also want SDK logs showing retry/backoff behavior.
jen-cs: Customer uploaded trace snippets and SDK logs to support ticket. Sample trace: 
```
frontend.accept -> 15ms
router.queue -> 2200ms
runtime.kv_fetch -> 1800ms
runtime.execute -> 120ms
```
Queue time correlates with SM saturation.
andrew: Short-term mitigation options: 1) Failover routing to alternate model variant on a different pool (if customer allows); 2) Temporarily throttle their concurrency at the gateway to smooth bursts; 3) Manually migrate to an isolated host (evict co-tenants). Need approval from POC.
mike: For root cause: check if slice crosstalk is due to GPU kernel launching patterns — concurrent small kernels from other tenant can saturate SM scheduler. Ask infra to pull `nvprof` style counters or ROCm perf counters. Also check whether KV cache misses amplified load (lots of full attention passes).
sophia: I'll ask Acme if they can lower batch size while we probe. Also requesting their recent job schedule (are they doing many short-lived jobs?).
infra-bot: Debug artifacts requested: node metrics link: https://infra.internal/metrics/node/eu2-dedicated-021?from=2025-11-02T14:10Z&to=2025-11-02T14:20Z , MIG configs: https://infra.internal/mig/eu2-dedicated-021 , autoscale logs: https://infra.internal/autoscale/attempts/3401234567.
mike: I'll grab kernel latency histograms and SM occupancy charts, tagging with those request_ids. If we see other tenants launching many small kernels, that's a noisy neighbor.
andrew: Also checking capacity control plane: quota-exhausted claim — operations, can you confirm if regional MIG templates were exhausted or if autoscaler had a transient credential error?
sophia: ops-cc: @andrew pinged ops. ops responded in ticket: "templates are low; provisioning backlog from recent fleet updates consumed spare templates. We can free 2 templates by reverting pending pre-builds but that will take ~12m."
jen-cs: Customer wants a timeline; they're on a revenue-impact plan. They asked for immediate mitigation (routing or temporary isolation).
mike: Short-term action list: reduce customer concurrency at gateway (rate-limit key) and enable failover routing to dedicated-fallback-pool-eu2; collect nv counters; examine KV miss rate. Long-term: investigate packing policy for MIG: consider tighter isolation (no co-tenants on same slice) for high-SLA reserved pools.
sophia: I'll message customer with mitigation steps and ETA: immediate concurrency cap applied in 2m, failover routing enabled 8m, ops to free templates ~12m.
jen-cs: Customer acknowledged, asked to keep them in loop. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Action created: INC-3401234567 assigned to eng-runtime (mike) and ops (andrew).
